summary: Cross-workspace Slack role propagation and Confluence space seed automation request
description:
Issue summary:
We need an automated mechanism to propagate role/group membership changes from the central directory to multiple Slack workspaces and simultaneously bootstrap a Confluence space with a small set of templated pages and initial permissions.

Impact:
Currently, when we update pod reviewer groups or oncall role mappings, engineers must manually update membership across three Slack workspaces and then request a Confluence space creation with manual permission granting. This causes delays in onboarding, inconsistent permissions, and occasional missing runbook pages during incident responses.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement an automation that listens for updates to the central group registry (LDAP/SCIM source) and propagates role changes to Slack workspaces: #runtime-ops, #model-evals, and #platform-pods.
- Create a Confluence space provisioning task that, when a new pod/team is onboarded, will create a space from a seed template containing: Incident Runbook, Oncall Roster, Playbooks, and Ownership page.
- Ensure the Confluence space creation sets space-level permissions aligned to the propagated Slack role (e.g., "pod-reviewers" => Confluence group pod-reviewers with edit access).
- Provide an audit log (linkable) showing which automation run applied which changes and an ability to rollback the latest change.
- Expose a one-click trigger in the internal admin console to run the provisioning for a team with a dry-run option.

Background/context:
This request comes from recent cross-pod incidents where runbooks were incomplete and channel membership lagged behind directory changes. We have an initial IAM mapping for groups, but no reliable propagation mechanism across multiple Slack workspaces or a templated Confluence scaffold. Existing manual process is error-prone and scales poorly as pods grow.

Proposed constraints and non-goals:
- We are not changing SCIM/LDAP itself; this should consume changes from the existing source of truth.
- This task should not attempt full org-wide Slack consolidation; only propagate mapped groups to listed workspaces.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Time-to-onboard new pod reduced from ~2 business days to <30 minutes for initial channel/space creation and role mapping (dry-run measured).
- Zero manual membership edits required for role changes in 90% of cases over a 30-day pilot.
- Confluence seed page completeness verification script reports 100% presence of required runbook pages after provisioning.

Notes for implementer:
- Use existing service account "infra-provisioner@redwood.com" and KMS for credential access.
- Keep change events idempotent and record run IDs in the audit log.
- Respect existing retention and data classification labels on Confluence spaces.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - administrative request; reproduction is a dry-run of provisioning using the admin console. Steps we want supported: 1) Select pod name in console. 2) Click 'Provision channels and space (dry-run)'. 3) Review proposed changes. 4) Click 'Apply'.

investigation_notes:
Initial investigation:
- Verified existing central group directory at identity.company.internal (SCIM enabled).
- Confirmed three target Slack workspaces are available with admin bot installed.
- Found rate limits on Confluence REST endpoint: ~30 creates/min default; applied for quota bump.
- Confirmed service account infra-provisioner has 'space creator' scope but not yet linked to audit sink.
- Hypotheses: throttling caused last-month manual failures; human error in mapping caused missing runbook pages.
Next steps: finish Confluence template review, wire admin console webhook, add audit logging integration.
resolution:
Work completed (partial):
- Implemented Slack role propagation service as a reconciler that pulls SCIM group membership diffs and applies membership changes to the three target workspaces. Runs every 5 minutes; idempotent.
- Built Confluence seeding task with template pages (Incident Runbook, Oncall Roster, Playbooks, Ownership). Scoped as 'incident-ready' template for runtime-ops pilot. Uses service account and writes change events to /audit/provisioning.
- Added dry-run mode and a one-click 'Apply' in internal admin console (prototype behind feature flag).
- Created rollback by recording pre-change snapshot and exposing a 'Revert last run' action for each run ID.

Open follow-ups:
- Complete security review of seeded page content for PII (assigned Jordan Kim).
- Monitor pilot for 30 days and collect metrics (PMs to instrument).
- Expand workspace list after pilot and document runbook for Platform Oncall.
